Information must arrive before a trade can use it

Predict: can a rule based on tonight’s close earn the return that happened before tonight’s close?

Original hypothetical teaching example. This complete static route needs no JavaScript or animation. The interactive walkthrough is available inside the chapter.

On a narrow screen, scroll the diagram horizontally. Every value and step is also explained below.

Step 4/4: Earn the holding-period return
The chosen position earns open[t+1]→open[t+2], then later signals control later intervals. Cash earns the declared cash rate.

All steps and numerical explanations

  1. Observe the close

    At day t close, the three required closes are now known. Earlier prices cannot be traded retroactively.

  2. Form the signal

    Compare close[t] with the trailing three-close mean. The signal uses no later close.

  3. Execute at the next open

    The earliest eligible trade in this lesson is open[t+1]. Pay the declared transaction cost at execution.

  4. Earn the holding-period return

    The chosen position earns open[t+1]→open[t+2], then later signals control later intervals. Cash earns the declared cash rate.

Illustrative lesson execution convention. Real delays, available liquidity and slippage may require a later or different execution model.
